title: Royalties, complimentary copies and the price of books
summary: Russell's Jelly Roll book, the copies owed to interviewees, and the cost of the Condon book.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Well, I don't know whether they could have been charged. They might have been charged. There was no, the first royalty was all used up anyway with the free copies that we had to give away. See, books like this, everybody wants copies of it. That's one reason I figured the Jelly Roll book, I'd better wait a few years until everybody's dead. I've promised so many copies. I've had over sixty interviews, and there are about a dozen people who wrote articles, some of them reprints like Charles Smith and Danny Barker and people of that kind. Anyway, most of those people will want copies of the book. We will. We'll pay for them, no? I mean, I would consider it an obligation of mine to furnish them with copies. If I'd figure out the royalties, it might be a twenty dollar book, actually, which would be about two dollars royalty. I figured he'd sell about four hundred copies, which would bring in about eight hundred dollars royalty I might get out of the book. And that would hardly pay for the, at the author's price, would hardly pay for the eighty copies of the book. I wasn't really worrying about them.
You could go to Preservation Hall and sell a thousand a night. Just sign your name on them. I know Squibb once said, they have orders for about four hundred from libraries.

It's about the main sale that they get. And all of us jazz fans would be too poor to buy a twenty dollar book anyway, hard and early. I got the Eddie Condon book the other day. How much did you have to pay for that book? It paid seven dollars or something. That's good. I paid seventeen fifty. Yeah seventeen fifty. So I never would have bought that if it, except it was less than half price. Did I ever tell you what Pickle Jackson told me?
He was helping me move and he said, if you read too many books it'll put a hole in your head.
Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.
Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. stuff

No, no, I wouldn't begrudge you giving these guys the books, but I did think it was sort of funny, though, that it would take the entire royalty, at least, to pay for the complimentary copies, so-called. In a way, they're not necessarily complimentary. They did their best to tell me what they knew and they deserve special treatment.
Some of the people that wrote Arkles, you've never given any money to.
You ought to at least give me a copy of the book, Russell. There we go.
